interest: This docket sheet provides valuable insight into pre-World War II diplomatic, military, and immigration frictions between the United States and Japan during late 1939 and early 1940. It highlights Japanese authorities' increasing scrutiny of American naval personnel and civilian passengers traveling on naval transports like the USS Gold Star between Guam and Japan, signaling mounting security tensions and tightening border controls. Furthermore, the references to the repatriation of Japanese Americans and consular requests for departure statistics from Honolulu and Pacific Coast ports illustrate U.S. official tracking of Nisei mobility and return migration to Japan on the eve of the Pacific War.
overview: This file consists of Sheet 1 of the Department of State's List of Papers (docket sheet) for decimal classification 894.5511 (Immigration to Japan from the United States), indexing correspondence and actions recorded between December 1939 and March 1940. The entries summarize communications from Richard F. Boyce, American Consul at Yokohama, regarding Japanese passport and entry regulations. Despatch No. 271 addresses stricter Japanese passport rules for passengers aboard the naval supply vessel USS Gold Star traveling to and from Guam, noting that landing on certificates of identity issued by the Governor of Guam would no longer be permitted without a consular guarantee. Despatch No. 475 and related memoranda concern the repatriation of Americans of Japanese ancestry, including an internal memorandum by Joseph W. Ballantine of the Division of Far Eastern Affairs and an inquiry to the Department of Labor requesting entry and departure statistics for Japanese Americans at Pacific Coast ports and Honolulu. Because the underlying despatches were cross-referenced and filed under other decimal numbers (such as 138/3635, 130-, and 394.117/), this docket sheet serves as the primary record under this subject classification.

subfiles.about: Docket sheet indexing State Department correspondence, memoranda, and interdepartmental requests regarding immigration to Japan from the United States between December 1939 and March 1940.
subfiles.summary: This docket sheet summarizes two despatches from Consul Richard F. Boyce in Yokohama and related internal Department actions. Sub No. 1 records despatch No. 271 of December 15, 1939, regarding Japanese passport requirements for passengers on the USS Gold Star at Guam and Japanese refusal to accept certificates of identity issued by the Governor of Guam without a consular guarantee. Sub No. 2 indexes despatch No. 475 of February 6, 1940, regarding the repatriation of Americans of Japanese race, along with a March 10 memorandum by Joseph W. Ballantine and a March 29 request to the Department of Labor for entry and departure statistics of Japanese Americans at Pacific Coast ports and Honolulu.
